articles.summary: QuestDB's new binary Wire Protocol vs InfluxDB Line Protocol in TSBS: 33M rows/s on one machine even at a million series, about 3.6x faster than ILP over a network.
articles.title: Introducing QuestDB's new binary ingestion protocol: QWP

articles.summary: QWP is QuestDB's binary, columnar wire protocol. One client streams both ingestion and SQL queries, dataframes and Arrow travel in both directions, and failover is built in.
articles.title: QWP: QuestDB's own binary wire protocol for ingestion and queries

articles.summary: QuestDB 10.0 ships QWP, a binary columnar protocol that both writes data in and streams Arrow back out, from a single client. It also brings live views in beta, notebooks driven by coding agents, and the storage work that QuestDB Enterprise 4.0 builds cold storage on.
articles.title: QuestDB 10.0: QWP, one binary streaming protocol for writes and Arrow reads

articles.summary: We built a naive parallel reader to see how fast QuestDB's new QWP protocol can stream query results into Arrow, compared it against ClickHouse and TimescaleDB, and stripped out three measurement artifacts before the numbers meant anything.
articles.title: Streaming 500 million rows into Apache Arrow in 2.3 seconds

articles.summary: Cold storage tiers ageing partitions to object storage and keeps them queryable, QWP moves data in and out faster, and failover no longer needs a restart.
articles.title: QuestDB Enterprise 4.0: cold storage, QWP, and restart-free failover
